This reaction is based on soda lime decarboxylation.

Given reaction:

CH3−CH2−COONa→NaOH/CaO, ΔA+Na2CO3CH_3-CH_2-COONa \xrightarrow{NaOH/CaO, \ \Delta} A + Na_2CO_3​

➡ Sodium propanoate (CH₃–CH₂–COONa), when heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO), undergoes decarboxylation.
➡ In this reaction, the –COONa group is removed and replaced by a hydrogen atom.

CH3−CH2−COONa  →NaOH/CaO, Δ  CH3−CH3+Na2CO3CH_3-CH_2-COONa \; \xrightarrow{NaOH/CaO, \ \Delta} \; CH_3-CH_3 + Na_2CO_3​

So,

A=CH3−CH3=EthaneA = CH_3-CH_3 = \textbf{Ethane}

questions.explanation:
Given:
3-methylbut-1-ene (CH₂=C(CH₃)-CH₂-CH₃) + HBr → X

Step 1: Identify the type of reaction.

  • This is electrophilic addition of HBr to an alkene.

  • Markovnikov’s rule applies: the H atom adds to the carbon of the double bond that already has more H atoms, and Br adds to the carbon with fewer H atoms.

Step 2: Apply Markovnikov’s rule.

  • Double bond is between C1 and C2.

  • C1 has 2 H, C2 has 1 H (since C2 is attached to CH₃).

  • H will add to C1, Br will add to C2.

Step 3: Write the product.

CH3​−C(Br)(CH3)−CH2​−CH3​

Final product: CH₃–C(I)(Cl)–CHD₂, Correct option: A.

Isomers of hexane, based on their branching, can be divided into three distinct classes as shown in the figure.

(I)  

(II)  

(III)  

The correct order of their boiling point is
questions.explanation:
1. Structure (III) is n-hexane: It's a straight-chain alkane. The text correctly states that it has the largest surface area, which leads to the strongest intermolecular forces (specifically, London dispersion forces) and therefore the highest boiling point.

2. Structure (II) is 2-methylpentane: This is a branched isomer with one branch. The text explains that it's more compact than n-hexane, resulting in a smaller surface area, weaker intermolecular forces, and a lower boiling point compared to n-hexane.

3. Structure (I) is 2,3-dimethylbutane: This is the most branched and most compact isomer. The text correctly identifies that this structure has the smallest surface area, the weakest intermolecular forces, and consequently, the lowest boiling point.

This corresponds to the order: III > II > I.
